title: Observation-only: the wal_wait alert is a single-sample artifact and no memory/storage knob is causal for the 0.8838 terminal share of the read-only GetUserTweets class

anomaly.aggregation: max over the measured window (median 0.0, p95 0.0)

configuration_cause: None of the incumbent's memory/storage knobs is causal for the flagged anomaly. (1) wal_sync_method=open_datasync makes every WAL write a device-synchronous O_DSYNC write, so the flush cost is folded into wal write latency and sync_average_ms is null by construction; the alert's slow-fsync branch therefore cannot be read directly off the counter set and must be judged from wal_timing.write_average_ms, wait events and host_io together. (2) commit_delay=671 with commit_siblings=12 is inert: with 8 terminals, numbackends max 9, active_backends median 6/p95 9 and idle_in_transaction max 5, the sibling gate is never reached, so no transaction is delayed and the pair cannot explain any tail. (3) checkpoint_timeout=100 with checkpoint_completion_target=0.833 and max_wal_size=3672 MB yielded only ~1 timed checkpoint per 161 s run, with checkpoint_write_time=checkpoint_sync_time=0 and buffers_checkpoint=6.56/s. (4) bgwriter_delay=22, bgwriter_lru_maxpages=338, bgwriter_flush_after=143, checkpoint_flush_after=177 and backend_flush_after=83 are bounded-writeback settings, yet buffers_clean=0/s with dirty_bytes median 3.45 MB and writeback_bytes p95 45 kB: there is nothing to write back. (5) shared_buffers=53504 pages (418 MB) is sufficient: buffer_hit_ratio 0.99993, blks_read 20.1/s, blk_read_time 0.20 ms/s. (6) work_mem=15776 kB and temp_buffers=10139 are never exercised: temp_files=0 and temp_bytes=0.
mechanism: Disk-side demand per client transaction is about one microsecond: wal_write_time_per_txn 0.0010384 ms, wal_bytes_per_txn 5.17 B, blk_read_time_per_txn 7.17e-6 ms, checkpoint_write_time_per_txn 0, checkpoint_sync_time_per_txn 0, temp_bytes_per_txn 0. Even at the per-write level the cost is small: 0.1379 ms x 212.7 WAL writes/s = 29.3 ms of device-synchronous write per second (2.9% of one core-second) with PSI io some/full stall fraction 0.0, io_waiting_backends p95 1/max 1 and exactly one instantaneous sample (wal_waiting_backends max 1 of ~9 backends) showing a WAL waiter. The throughput-limiting class GetUserTweets (3,048,834 of ~3.42M transactions, terminal_capacity_fraction 0.8838) is read-only and therefore never enqueues on the WAL flush path at all; its mean (278 us) exceeds its median (169 us) because of a non-storage p99 (2813 us) that no allowed memory/storage knob can address. The smallest coherent knob group for the storage mechanism actually diagnosed here is the empty set: any edit to wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay/flush_after, wal_sync_method, commit_delay/commit_siblings, bgwriter pacing or checkpoint spacing would be an unfalsifiable perturbation of a subsystem currently delivering microseconds of work per transaction.

intermediate_metrics.aggregation: class total latency / (terminals x measured seconds)

query_effect: No plan or access-path change: plan_evidence is an Index Scan (estimated_rows 1, cost 8.45) with 9.67 buffer hits and 7.1e-4 block reads per transaction, and no memory/storage knob in the allowed set alters access-path selection for GetUserTweets or the InsertTweet insert path. Expected query effect: none.
expected_tps_effect: No change is expected from the memory/storage domain. A re-measurement should land inside the incumbent's own replicate band (28257.5-31906.7 goodput_rps, verified median 30213.6), i.e. within +-10%. The only lever that could move TPS is the non-storage tail of GetUserTweets, which is outside this domain.
expected_latency_effect: None for GetUserTweets (p50 169 us / p99 2813 us are cache-resident, executor-side micro-stalls on a read-only class), and no measurable effect for InsertTweet, whose p99 of 3999 us is not fsync-bound when the entire WAL write budget is ~1 us per client transaction and the per-write device latency is 0.138 ms.

predictions.rationale: Closed-loop identity 8 terminals / ~283 us weighted mean latency reproduces the observed 28257 rps; with knob_changes=[] the re-measurement must stay inside the incumbent's own replicate band (28257.5-31906.7 rps, verified median 30213.6). A +-10% window brackets the 12.9% max/min spread already observed across the three incumbent replicates.

GetUserTweets consumed 0.8838 of terminal capacity (incumbent replicates 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787; span 0.51 pp) at a 169 us median while its storage cost is 7.2e-6 ms of block read time and 0 temp bytes per transaction; this read-only class never touches the WAL, checkpoint or bgwriter paths, so no allowed memory/storage knob can shift the fraction by 1 pp.

Measured 0.1379 ms mean per WAL write with host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0, blk_read_time 0.2027 ms/s and checkpoint write/sync time 0. The WAL write path has no queue to relieve (212.7 writes/s, 146.1 kB/s), so the mean per-write latency should not move by 0.5 ms.

The flagged wait is a single instantaneous sample: median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 of ~9 backends over 148 samples. Reconfiguring an unstressed WAL pipeline cannot remove a waiter that is not present beyond the noise floor, so the max should not rise by 1 backend or more.

InsertTweet p99 is 3999 us on 0.0075 WAL writes and 5.17 WAL bytes per client transaction, with the whole WAL write budget at ~1 us per client transaction and no recorded fsync time (sync_average_ms null because open_datasync folds the flush into write). The commit durability path is not the tail driver, so its p99 should stay within the +-20% span already observed across replicates (3336-3999 us).

alternatives.statement: The 0.1379 ms mean WAL write latency is an under-sampled device flush cost: because wal_sync_method=open_datasync folds the fsync into write() and sync_average_ms is null, the wal_wait alert could be the leading edge of a storage-latency mechanism that grows with writer concurrency.
The 2813 us p99 of GetUserTweets is backend clock-sweep eviction of dirty buffers stalling readers that pin the same pages, i.e. background-writer/checkpoint pacing rather than the WAL path.

The observation run's 28257 rps versus 29762.6-31906.7 rps across the incumbent replicates is client/terminal-side variance (idle_in_transaction p95 3 / max 5, client_waiting_backends p95 4 of 9 backends), not a server memory/storage effect.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: per-class wait_event sampling plus EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for the exact GetUserTweets SQL to attribute the 2813 us p99 to executor/LWLock/client effects before any storage knob is considered.
concurrency_maintenance: confirm that the 0.8838 terminal share is a frequency effect (no lock waits, conflicts 0.0, locks_waiting 0) so that no maintenance knob is proposed against it.
why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not claim to exceed the incumbent; it prevents an evidence-free reconfiguration of an unstressed storage subsystem (wal_buffers, wal_sync_method, commit_delay/commit_siblings, bgwriter/checkpoint spacing) that would consume measurement budget and could perturb the very tail that limits TPS. Its value is diagnostic: it converts the high-severity wal_wait alert into a falsifiable, zero-cost statement (wal_write_time_per_txn ~1 us, write_average_ms 0.138, PSI io stalls 0.0, one waiter sample) so that the remaining budget goes to the path that actually owns 0.8838 of terminal capacity.
